analysis: The only change is in .github/workflows/ci.yml, head lines 154-157: a new step in the test-provider job runs `python3 scripts/test-desktop-api.py provider-swift/.build/debug/darkbloom`. It is gated on `!cancelled()` and a successful provider-ci-build, and has a 3-minute timeout. It adds no secrets, no new permissions (workflow-level `contents: read` is unchanged), no new third-party actions and no changes to artifact upload or cache. It does not touch any pinned action SHAs. The step runs after the diagnostics upload and before the MiMo native gates. Because the gating is based on the build outcome rather than on earlier test steps, it cannot mask failures in other steps, and its own failure is reported independently. The step touches no coordinator or provider wire/custody boundary and no attestation or authorization path, so the TB-002, TB-009 and TB-011 controls are unaffected. The threat-model scope covers the provider/native runtime and consumed contracts, and this change is CI test plumbing only. The test name implies a desktop control API with isolated local state. Unverified contract: scripts/test-desktop-api.py and any desktop control API in the provider binary are not in the supplied evidence. A new local control surface, if added by this PR in other files, would be a candidate for TB-003 local-operator and credential-custody review in other batches. This workflow step provides no evidence of a regression. One residual point: the step runs the debug binary under LLVM_PROFILE_FILE coverage env, which only adds profraw files. There is nothing security-relevant here.
